advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm no list_filters (or downstream) assertion relies on the store's `.env-id` matching the env_id of the pre-seeded ticket events after per-test reminting.
evidence: tests/interfaces/queries/test_list_filters.py:82-88: seeding writes committed events under the template's identity before the per-test copy
tests/_topology_template.py:160-167: `_remint_store_identities` unconditionally writes a fresh uuid to `.env-id`
src/rebar/_store/env_identity.py:90: `# ... It only runs when \`.env-id\` is ABSENT ...` so reminting to a new value silently no-ops the guard, leaving copy env-id != seeded events' env_id
advisory.finding: The list_filters template now seeds the ticket scenario into the session-scoped store BEFORE cloning, and clone_topology_template remints `.env-id` to a fresh random uuid on every copy. The reminted env-id therefore no longer matches the env_id stamped into the pre-seeded event files (the re-identification guard does not fire because it only runs when `.env-id` is ABSENT). This pre-seed-then-remint combination is new (the old rebar_repo template was not pre-seeded); verify no filter/authorship assertion depends on env-id/event consistency.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that places a symlink whose target embeds the source topology root into a template, clones it, and asserts the copy's symlink is rebased to the copy root (and that _assert_source_paths_absent catches an unrebased one).
evidence: tests/_topology_template.py:130 `if path.is_symlink():` then `path.unlink(); path.symlink_to(rewritten)` — the rewrite branch
tests/_topology_template.py:165 `_assert_source_paths_absent` symlink branch: `if any(source in os.fsencode(os.readlink(path)) ...)`

search of tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py for `symlink`: all hits are `copytree(..., symlinks=True)` or `not path.is_symlink()` filters — no test creates a symlink embedding a source path

ABSENCE: test_copy_repoints_sibling_origin_and_keeps_refs_isolated (tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py:220+) builds bare repos and remotes only; the final offender scan at line 299 explicitly skips symlinks (`not path.is_symlink()`), so even that assertion cannot witness a symlink regression
advisory.finding: The new symlink-target rewriting behavior in clone_topology_template (the path.is_symlink() branch of _rewrite_embedded_paths that unlinks and recreates a symlink with a rewritten target, and the symlink branch of _assert_source_paths_absent) has no test. The added isolation test only constructs ordinary files and bare repos; no topology under test contains a symlink whose target embeds the source topology root, so a regression that broke symlink rewriting or its absence-check would pass undetected.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Rewrite/assert both the resolved AND the as-given (unresolved) template path so verbatim-stored git remote URLs are relocated even when the tmp root is symlinked.
evidence: tests/_topology_template.py:171: `source_paths = {source for source, _destination in rewrites}` (guard also keyed on resolved bytes only)
tests/integration/test_prepare_reclaim_backup.py:124 (analogous): remote/origin recorded via `str(remote)` — an unresolved absolute path — so config bytes may not equal template.resolve()
The fixtures set the origin using the literal (possibly unresolved) path passed into the builder, while the rewrite/guard use .resolve().
dropped.finding: clone_topology_template rewrites embedded paths using the RESOLVED template/destination paths (os.fsencode(template.resolve())), but git stores remote URLs and clone origins verbatim as given (unresolved). When the template lives under a path whose real form differs from its resolved form (e.g. a symlinked tmpdir such as macOS /var -> /private/var), a sibling `origin` URL recorded in unresolved form is neither rewritten by _rewrite_embedded_paths nor detected by _assert_source_paths_absent (which also searches only for the resolved bytes), leaving the copy pointed at the template's remote.
